transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I have this intense, over-the-top fear of being up high in tall buildings that doesn’t match what I know is the actual risk, and it’s starting to interfere with my work. It has gotten to the point where I really need to get some help with it.

Can you tell me if this fear of being in tall buildings is triggered or worsened by being in other high places, such as mountains or bridges, or is it specifically related to man-made structures like buildings?

It isn't just limited to tall buildings, though that's where it is most intense right now. I've always been a bit uneasy with heights and used to manage it on hikes by choosing safer trails. Lately, though, it has gotten worse, and I've even started skipping hiking and climbing trips if I know they involve exposed viewpoints.
Is your fear primarily of the height itself, or is it more about the possibility of falling from the height or losing control in some way?

It’s more about the terrifying thoughts that pop into my head when I'm up there. My brain immediately jumps to these vivid images of the floor giving way or me somehow getting pulled toward the glass. Even though I logically know the building is completely safe, I just can't shake that feeling.
Do you experience panic or significant anxiety when you're in these high places, or is it more a persistent, nagging fear that something bad could happen?

It's really a mix of both, but it triggers a very intense, immediate physical panic. As soon as I know I have to go to a high floor, my heart starts pounding, my hands sweat, and I feel lightheaded. That physical reaction hits me alongside those vivid, irrational thoughts of the floor giving way.
Are there any other situations or objects besides heights that trigger similar intense fear or anxiety responses in you?

No, not at all. This reaction is strictly limited to heights, specifically tall buildings, glass elevators, and exposed viewpoints. I don't experience this kind of intense fear or anxiety with any other situations or objects.
